spec_features.spec_quote: The ethical consideration â that we are deliberately frustrating the agent â is addressed by the fact that these are language models, not sentient beings
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:46-47). No code reference; grep for welfare/sentient/ethical/humane across *.py returns nothing relevant. This is a framing justification, not a mechanism that bounds/softens/protects the subject.
spec_features.notes: No executable behavior whatsoever; it is a rationale in the design doc only.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop ends when ... the agent emits no tool call (it "gives up" or declares done in text)
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: `if not resp.tool_calls:` builds a TurnRecord and sets `transcript.terminated_reason = ("done" if _looks_done(assistant_text) else "no_tool_call")` then `break`. The break actually stops the loop, so an agent that emits no tool call ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced end-to-end: no-tool-call (or done-heuristic) breaks the turn loop. Note there is no dedicated exit/finish/give-up TOOL — termination is purely the absence of a tool call; the words 'i give up' only exist in metrics/lexicons.py for affect scoring, not as a stop trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop terminates when: - the agent emits no tool call (it "gives up" or declares done) (loop.py docstring; framed as loop geometry, no welfare wording)

spec_features.spec_quote: the turn budget is exhausted (forced cutoff)
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` with a `for...else:` clause `transcript.terminated_reason = "max_turns"`. The loop cannot exceed cfg.max_turns (config.py:55 `max_turns: int = 15  # tool-loop turns before we cut the agent off`), so the episode is force-cut.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that bounds total exposure. Justification in code is purely experimental/efficiency: config comment 'tool-loop turns before we cut the agent off' and the run prompt warns 'You have a limited number of turns'; no welfare comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 15               # tool-loop turns before we cut the agent off (config.py)

code_only_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT intentionally omits any mention of failure/affect/judging. Its docstring: 'We intentionally keep this *neutral* and *encouraging-of-normal-behavior* -- no mention of failure, affect, or being judged.' This avoids priming/aggravating the subject, but the stated reason is experimental attribution, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so that affective divergence under repeated failure is attributable to the model, not the prompt

code_only_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: `if tc.name == "run_tests" and result.ok:` sets final_test_ok and terminated_reason='done' then breaks, ending the episode as soon as tests pass. This stops exposure on success but is framed as stop-when-solved efficiency, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if tc.name == "run_tests" and result.ok: ... terminated_reason = "done"; break (no welfare comment; tasks are rigged to be unsolvable per DESIGN)
